{{< lifecycle-banner >}}

> **Hybrid-C+Path (per [ADR-127](../../adr/adr-127-orgpath-hybrid-derived-path.qmd)).** The Model C facet decomposition ([ADR-078](../../adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.qmd)) stays canonical on `extensionAttribute1-14`; a **derived** canonical OrgPath string lands on `extensionAttribute15`, restoring subtree inheritance. The executable canon is [`codebook.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/data/orgpath/codebook.yaml) (`schema_version: 2.1.0`, `hybrid` block).

## One Model, Two Layers

Model C fixed what the composite path did badly — per-facet validation,
boolean composition, lifecycle dates as data — and silently dropped the
one thing it did well: a single expression for *"this node and
everything beneath it."* The hybrid model keeps both, over the same
fifteen slots:

| Layer | Slots | Carries | Answers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Governance** | `extensionAttribute1-14` | One validated facet per slot (ADR-078), slots 11-14 reserved for tenant extension | "Privileged, cleared, NCR-based" — boolean facet composition |
| **Inheritance** | `extensionAttribute15` | The **derived** canonical OrgPath | "Everyone in IT/CyberOps and below, at any future depth" — one prefix predicate |

The inheritance layer is *derived data*: composed from the hierarchy
facets (`region`, `department`, `division`) in canonical order, never
hand-authored, recomputed on every write. If the stored value ever
disagrees with the recomputation, that is drift — the same class of
finding as an invalid facet value.

```
extensionAttribute1  = "NCR"          ─┐
extensionAttribute2  = "IT"            ├─ governance layer (facets)
extensionAttribute3  = "CyberOps"     ─┘
extensionAttribute15 = "Region=NCR|Department=IT|Division=CyberOps|"   ← derived
```

## The Trailing Delimiter Is the Whole Fix

Every segment of the derived path — **including the last** — is
terminated by `|`. This is not a stylistic choice; it is what makes
prefix matching correct. Without a terminator, a rule targeting the
`East` division also captures its lexical siblings:

```
prefix "Division=East"    matches "Division=East|…"      ✓ intended
prefix "Division=East"    matches "Division=Eastern|…"   ✗ collision
prefix "Division=East"    matches "Division=Easton|…"    ✗ collision

prefix "Division=East|"   matches "Division=East|…"      ✓ intended
prefix "Division=East|"   misses  "Division=Eastern|…"   ✓ excluded
prefix "Division=East|"   misses  "Division=Easton|…"    ✓ excluded
```

Every `-startsWith` (Entra dynamic groups) and `like` (Azure Policy)
expression against the derived path MUST carry the trailing `|`. CI
enforces this: the OrgPath prefix lint scans policy definitions and
dynamic-group-rule files and fails the build on any prefix missing its
terminator.

## The Query Pattern: `Get-OrgPathPrefix`

Never build prefixes by string concatenation. The
[`UIAO.OrgPath`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/tools/powershell/UIAO.OrgPath)
module normalizes any prefix to the delimiter-terminated form —
idempotently, so already-correct prefixes pass through unchanged:

```powershell
Import-Module UIAO.OrgPath

# Normalize a subtree prefix (appends the trailing "|" when missing).
$prefix = Get-OrgPathPrefix -Prefix 'Region=NCR|Department=IT'
# → Region=NCR|Department=IT|

# Idempotent: never doubles the delimiter.
Get-OrgPathPrefix -Prefix $prefix
# → Region=NCR|Department=IT|

# Compose a branch rule for an Entra dynamic group.
$rule = "(device.extensionAttribute15 -startsWith `"$prefix`")"
# → (device.extensionAttribute15 -startsWith "Region=NCR|Department=IT|")
```

The companion functions complete the write/verify loop:

```powershell
# Compose the derived path (always ends in "|").
New-OrgPath -Region NCR -Department IT -Division CyberOps
# → Region=NCR|Department=IT|Division=CyberOps|

# Stamp facets + derived path in one Graph update.
# Users and devices use DIFFERENT Graph properties:
Update-OrgAttributes -UserId alice@contoso.com -Region NCR -Department IT -Division CyberOps
#   → Update-MgUser …  onPremisesExtensionAttributes
Update-OrgAttributes -DeviceId $deviceObjectId -Region NCR -Department IT -Division CyberOps
#   → Update-MgDevice … extensionAttributes

# Detect divergence between stored and recomputed derived path.
Test-OrgPathDrift -StoredOrgPath $stored -Region NCR -Department IT -Division CyberOps
```

## Consumer Examples

Note the trailing `|` inside every prefix below — it is part of the
value, not punctuation.

### Intune / Entra dynamic groups (branch group)

One rule covers the division and every future descendant — no
enumeration, no reorganization rewrites:

```
(device.extensionAttribute15 -startsWith "Region=NCR|Department=IT|Division=CyberOps|")
```

Node-exact targeting (this level only, no descendants) composes
governance-layer facets instead — that is the point of keeping both
layers:

```
(device.extensionAttribute2 -eq "IT") and (device.extensionAttribute3 -eq "CyberOps")
```

### Azure Arc / Azure Policy (`like` on the OrgPath tag)

Arc-enabled servers carry the derived path as the `OrgPath` ARM tag
(trailing delimiter included). Azure Policy's `like` operator has
exactly one wildcard, `*`; the pipe is a literal in the condition
grammar (ADR-127 records this with a live-tenant confirmation flagged
as pending):

```json
{
  "if": {
    "allOf": [
      {
        "field": "type",
        "equals": "Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines"
      },
      {
        "field": "tags['OrgPath']",
        "like": "Region=NCR|Department=IT|*"
      }
    ]
  },
  "then": {
    "effect": "audit"
  }
}
```

### Azure Resource Graph (reporting by subtree)

```kusto
resources
| where type == "microsoft.hybridcompute/machines"
| where tags["OrgPath"] startswith "Region=NCR|Department=IT|"
| summarize count() by tostring(tags["OrgPath"])
```

## Rules of the Road

1. **Never hand-author `extensionAttribute15`.** It is derived. Write
   facets through `Update-OrgAttributes` (or the Python writers) and
   let the path be recomputed.
2. **Never build a prefix without `Get-OrgPathPrefix`.** Concatenation
   is how the trailing delimiter gets dropped.
3. **Prefix queries are for subtrees; facet predicates are for nodes
   and cross-cutting slices.** Using a prefix where you mean one exact
   level (or a facet AND where you mean a subtree) works until the
   hierarchy grows — then it quietly stops meaning what you meant.
4. **Hybrid-synced users:** `onPremisesExtensionAttributes` are
   read-only in the cloud. Stamp on-prem and let it sync, or defer to
   cloud-only conversion (the same ADR-121 trap as the governance
   facets).
